The minimum is 39 rounds. The lower bound is proved below; I did not construct a schedule reaching it, so the match with 39 rests on my recollection of this problem's known answer.

**Lower bound.** In each round a player plays exactly one opponent. Each player must meet 39 different opponents, so at least 39 rounds are needed.

**Achievability (not verified).** One way to view the movement is as 40 "slots" arranged on a cycle. Each court has an "up" slot and a "down" slot, so the cycle is courts 1 to 20 going up, then 20 to 1 going down. Every round, each slot advances one step along the cycle. The two players on a court occupy opposite slots, and the winner takes the up slot while the loser takes the down slot. Because the winner of each match can be chosen freely, there is enough freedom in how players move between slots to arrange for everyone to meet everyone within 39 rounds. I did not carry out this construction explicitly.

ANSWER: 39
